tracks.narration: An amplifier with a voltage gain of one — what could that possibly be good for?
Drive the base, take the output off the emitter. The collector ties straight to V C C, and an emitter resistor pulls the emitter down to ground.
The base-emitter junction always drops about zero point seven volts when conducting. So the emitter voltage tracks the base — just shifted down by V B E.
Wiggle the input. The output traces the same wiggle, half a volt below it. Voltage gain is one — but the current swung into the load is beta times bigger than the current the source had to give.
High input impedance, low output impedance, current to spare — the emitter follower is the buffer that drives the speaker, the cable, the next stage.
